statement: Get characters to their subclass at Desert Dunes before anything else on arriving in World 2.
First three characters should be Bowman Barbarian and Shaman because they focus on World 2 skills alchemy catching and fishing.
Next three characters can be Hunter Squire and Wizard since they will be used in World 3.
If you get a seventh character before World 3 make it the secret class Journeyman.
Click the cauldron then click a character to add them; this starts brewing liquids.
Upgrade the cauldron to unlock new bubbles.
Characters assigned to the cauldron gain XP for as long as they are assigned.
Two bubble types: small passive bubbles and equippable big bubbles; only two big bubbles can be equipped at the moment.
Click the big bubble then click the character on the right that you want to assign it to.
Vials are alchemy buffs unlocked by dropping items in front of the cauldron; they are super easy to level.
Get vials to level 4 plus for the Shaman's damage.
Spend money in the Pay to Win tab to speed up alchemy; water upgrades early then cauldron upgrades later for luck and speed.
Do not skip alchemy; it is about 80 percent of account progression so learn the upgrades.
Orange 7 (FMJ) and green 7 (Shaker C) bubbles are huge to upgrade; unlock ASAP for accuracy and defense in beginning progression.
First green bubble Hammer lets you produce one extra item in the production tab.
Buy a couple of distilled water a day from the Alchemy Shop in the liquid tab; it is super beneficial.
At level 30 you get a second preset; set each character with one skilling and one combat preset.
Hybrid builds are not viable in this game.
Skilling build for Shaman should put points into Bubble Breakthrough which raises chance of unlocking a new bubble when brewing.
Catching is Bowman's specialty and works like chopping and mining in world one.
Fishing is Barbarian's specialty and produces four types of fish based on skill efficiency and equipped rods and lures set at the tackle rack.
Different pawns have different percentages of collecting fish which can be checked in the AFK info.
He links a site with early game builds for allocating points for combat and skilling.
Merits are a new mechanic; earn achievements from task challenges and each world has tasks that earn merits for its upgrades.
A merit shop NPC (like Grassland Gary in world one) exists in each town.
Bottom right of the task menu has guild dailies; completing them counts toward daily GP.
Most important world one merits: at least one hemoglobin boss keys mini boss talents mob respawn and Amarok armor.
Amarok armor besides the helmet is one of the cheapest defensive progression and hemoglobin helps survivability without relying on food.
Chemo (hemoglobin?) is required to progress in World 3 and sometimes the later half of World 2.
World 2 merit priority is at least mini boss talents and boss gems followed by mob respawn; Obel armor is optional.
Armor is optional going forward since you change to platinum in World 3.
Don't build gold armor since it only upgrades into nothing besides completing one quest.
Farming achievements unlocks recipes at top right; unlock tools and weapons first.
Stay away from free gems until you have more than enough.
Unlock icing iron bites recipe because it is used for a boss quest.
Owl menu is super late game but now starts dropping so you can get small gains little by little.
Post Office quest requires crafting boxes under Anvil tab 2 then gives daily quests for each resource collected.
You don't need to do all post office quests daily; uncompleted ones refresh in three days.
Spending boxes is big and he has a whole guide about it.
Arcade is not super important for early progression but nice for free jabs and candies.
Spend golden balls on upgrades on rotation.
Each week Killroy gives a challenge to kill monsters for skulls spent in his shop and it is a major boost later.
Until World 3 spend skulls on arcade bowls time candy and dungeon dice.
Get at least one black pearl and one white pearl for looty for Hunter's damage.
Killroy resets each week so you cannot stockpile skulls or purchases.
Mini boss in Birch Enclave spawns hourly and can drop recipe for serrated Rex ring an upgrade over party dungeon shop Rex ring.
Serrated Rex ring is better than steel bands.
Rings with skill efficiency percent should be kept for your skilling build once you get a new upgrade.
Farming the mini boss at the Coliseum drops the second best money card in the game.
Sewers monsters are super strong early so good armor is a must; boss Dr Defragmenter drops a super good damage percent card.
Above the sewer boss is a secret room; drop bolt cutters from green mushrooms to get another good card.
Googly eyes crafted item uses a recipe dropped from crab cakes; boss item drops next to the Kalo; boss is good for time candy and gems.
King Doot unlocked with Duke Jed eye recipe dropped by sand giants; portal is on the Sands of Time map.
Need one each of Archer Warrior and Mage on the map at once then talk to statues to spawn boss; drops gems and time candy.
Coliseum at Mimical gives another daily coliseum ticket.
Bottom of Coliseum map has a portal to Bandit Bob's Hideout where the World 2 party dungeon is located.
Do the main story quest and obstacle quest for stamps and keep leveling stamps up.
Buy the golden sculptor tool from World 2 shop and drop it at the marble NPC to turn the statue gold.
Gold statue lets you buy upgrades for statues (countdown unclear).
Pick up the tarantulite necklace at the Forest Villa; very good early game necklace.
Target gear: iron or platinum helmet Amarok chest legs and feet tarantulite necklace highest weapon and two serrated Rex rings; enough for World 3.
Progress to Efaunt and do the quest requiring ghosts to drop and unlock icing iron bites.
Enter Efaunt's domain slap all his hands then punch him in the face; collect the gem and hand it to the bird.
Nothing in IdleOn can be explained in five minutes; the game is complex but it connects like clockwork.
IdleOn is a marathon not a race so don't get overwhelmed.
